lesson.title: Review Day: Comparing Texts Across Genres
lesson.subject: ela

contentBlocks.text: This week you compared fiction and nonfiction closely. Let's review it all!

Quick review: fiction and nonfiction are two different genres (Day 1). You compared their purposes: entertaining story vs. informative facts (Day 2). You compared their point of view: individual vs. general (Day 3). You combined both into a fuller understanding (Day 4). Answer: what genre tells a made-up story, and what genre gives real facts? Name one thing each genre is especially good at showing you.
Wonderful work this week — you compared, contrasted, and combined two real genres on one topic! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review genre, purpose, point of view, and synthesis across fiction and nonfiction
Define fiction and nonfiction and state what each is especially good at showing
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child answer both review questions.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of genre comparison!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just one of the two review questions, whichever the child engaged with most this week
Ready for more: ask the child what other topics they'd like to compare across fiction and nonfiction in the future
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's four skills (genre definition, purpose, point of view, or synthesis) needs the most reinforcement before the next genre-comparison unit
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a recall and review activity — check that the child correctly identifies fiction as made-up stories and nonfiction as real facts, and states a genuine strength of each (fiction: emotional/personal experience; nonfiction: broad, factual information).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's Common Core Grade 5 Reading standards (RL.5.9/RI.5.9) before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.

generationData.instructions: Answer each question to review this week.
